chitchat: Sit on the bed, not the table.
Show me. Don't tell me, show me.
It'll scar. Everything scars. Scars are fine.
I have got one of everything and two of nothing.
If it's the teeth, I'm sorry in advance.
description: A tall woman with her sleeves cut off at the elbow, writing in a book with the stub of a pencil. Every surface in the room has been scrubbed within an hour. She finishes the sentence before she looks up, and looks up at the part of you that's wrong before she looks at your face.

options.label: You could fix a lot of that with better gear.

alone.text:
"For everything, yes."

She closes the book.

"Two hundred and eleven people. Babies, backs, burns, teeth, the ones that are going to die and the ones that only think they are. There's a girl of nineteen who's learning it and she's quick and she's four years off, and I'm fifty-eight."

"That's the only sum in this place that frightens anybody. Nobody talks about it. I'm telling you because you aren't from here, so it costs me nothing."

bye.text:
"Mind how you go."

She is already writing the next line in the book.

chrome.text:
She looks at you for slightly too long.

"I could." A beat. "Don't say that at the table."

And she opens the book again, and writes the sentence she was going to write, and doesn't say another word about it.

root.first: "Are you bleeding?" It's the first thing she says and it isn't rhetorical. "No. Right. Then sit down and don't touch anything."

options.label: You could fix a lot of that with better gear.

text_by_relation.close: "Ah." She puts the pencil down, which for her is dropping everything.
text_by_relation.familiar: "Sit down. How is the thing." She doesn't say which thing and doesn't need to.
text_by_relation.known: "You. Still upright." She goes back to the book.

clothing_layers: a shirt with the cuffs cut off

name: Mercy Vantry
